dashboard.label: Setup
dashboard.description: Import the first vulnerability feed. Everything else can wait.

div.h3: One thing to do: import a vulnerability feed
div.p: Riskability has no route to the internet and does not want one. The vulnerability data is a bundle you build on a connected machine and carry across. Until one is imported the app can assess nothing, and every count it shows is zero for that reason rather than because the fleet is clean.

Import one below and this setup page is done with. Everything else is optional and configured later, under the Administration menu: AI analysis, escalation rules and the firewall data source all ship off.

This needs an administrator. The controls below write through Splunk's configuration service and are gated on capabilities granted to admin and sc_admin, so a user without them will see the panel refuse rather than fail quietly.

div.h3: Building the bundle, on a machine that does have internet
div.pre:
riskability-feed sources # what can be fetched
riskability-feed build --out riskability-feed.tar.gz \ --ecosystem Ubuntu --ecosystem Debian --ecosystem Alpine \ --ecosystem npm --ecosystem PyPI --ecosystem Go --ecosystem Maven \ --kev --epss
div.p: Only the sources you name are downloaded. Pick the distributions and language ecosystems your fleet runs. A Windows estate also needs NVD, which carries the CPE-keyed ranges a registry version can be matched against: add --nvd 2015-2026 --mitre.
The full guidance, including what each source costs to carry and how redistribution licensing works, is on Administration → Feed administration once this page is done.
